title: ldap: connect to the address libcurl already resolved, not the hostname
body:
The legacy LDAP backend called Curl_conn_get_ip_info() to learn the
destination libcurl's connection layer had selected, but only used
ipquad.remote_port from it. ldap_init()/ldap_sslinit() were still called
with conn->origin->hostname, so the native LDAP SDK resolved and
connected to that hostname entirely on its own, independently of any
cfilter, CURLOPT_RESOLVE, or CURLOPT_CONNECT_TO decision. An application
pinning an LDAP hostname via CURLOPT_RESOLVE for SSRF protection got
that pin silently ignored.

For plain-text ldap:// connections, pass the already-resolved address
(ipquad.remote_ip) instead of the hostname, so the SDK connects to
exactly what libcurl decided. Empirically verified against a local slapd
(OpenLDAP 2.7.1): a CURLOPT_RESOLVE-pinned hostname that cannot be
resolved by the system resolver at all now still connects and completes
a search, whereas before the fix the SDK's independent re-resolution of
that hostname failed outright.

ldaps:// connections keep using the hostname: the legacy backend hands
ldaps:// TLS entirely to the native LDAP SDK (see the existing
CURLOPT_CAINFO/CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER/CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY/
CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYSTATUS notes for this same backend), and the SDK
verifies the server certificate against whatever host string it was
given, so switching to an IP literal there would break certificate
verification instead of just fixing destination selection. Documented as
a caveat on CURLOPT_RESOLVE and CURLOPT_CONNECT_TO instead.

Reported-by: Joshua Rogers

---

- [ ] amend the documentation update in the spirit of 70c084a0123b468fe7078e3fc72c78e1b66394b6 #23303

files.patch:
@@ -79,6 +79,14 @@ a transfer before you call curl_slist_free_all(3) on the list.
 Using this option multiple times makes the last set list override the previous
 ones. Set it to NULL to disable its use again.
 
+This option has no effect on ldaps:// requests when libcurl uses the legacy
+LDAP backend. That backend hands the connection to the native LDAP SDK,
+which independently resolves and connects to the original hostname for its
+TLS handshake. Plain-text ldap:// requests connect to the address this
+option selects. When libcurl is built with USE_OPENLDAP, the OpenLDAP
+backend routes the connection through curl's connection layer and this
+option is honored for both schemes.
+
 # DEFAULT
 
 NULL
